public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 581

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/581](https://www.erdosproblems.com/581)
- [CEG79] Chung, F. R. K. and Erdős, P. and Graham, R. L., _On the product of the point and line
  covering numbers of a graph_. Second International Conference on Combinatorial Mathematics
  (New York, 1978) (1979), 597-602.
- [Al96] Alon, Noga, _Bipartite subgraphs_. Combinatorica (1996), 301-311.
-/

@[expose] public section

open SimpleGraph

namespace Erdos581

/-- `f m` is the maximal `k` such that every triangle-free graph on `m` edges contains a
bipartite subgraph with `k` edges. -/
noncomputable def f (m : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sSup {k | ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V), G.CliqueFree 3 →
    G.edgeSet.ncard = m → ∃ H ≤ G, H.IsBipartite ∧ k ≤ H.edgeSet.ncard}

/--
Let $f(m)$ be the maximal $k$ such that a triangle-free graph on $m$ edges must contain a
bipartite graph with $k$ edges. Determine $f(m)$.

Resolved by Alon [Al96], who showed that there exist constants $c_1,c_2>0$ such that
$$\frac{m}{2}+c_1m^{4/5}\leq f(m)\leq \frac{m}{2}+c_2m^{4/5}.$$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos581.lean#L31"]
theorem erdos_581 : ∃ c₁ c₂ : ℝ, 0 < c₁ ∧ 0 < c₂ ∧ ∀ m : ℕ,
    (m : ℝ) / 2 + c₁ * (m : ℝ) ^ (4 / 5 : ℝ) ≤ f m ∧
      (f m : ℝ) ≤ (m : ℝ) / 2 + c₂ * (m : ℝ) ^ (4 / 5 : ℝ) := by
  sorry

end Erdos581

findings.description: The module-level reference [CEG79] (lines 25–27) points to an unrelated paper. Chung–Erdős–Graham, “On the product of the point and line covering numbers of a graph,” studies extrema of the product of vertex- and edge-cover numbers, followed by a hypergraph generalization; it does not pose the triangle-free bipartite-subgraph problem. This is a bibliographic slip only: the definition and theorem agree with Alon's cited result.
findings.source_evidence: The cited paper, https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1979-16.pdf, pp. 597–602, defines α₀(G) and α₁(G) as point and line covering numbers and studies α₀(G)α₁(G). A relevant original source is instead Erdős, “Problems and results in graph theory and combinatorial analysis” (1979), §8, pp. 159–161, https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1979-17.pdf: it defines the largest guaranteed bipartite-subgraph edge count and discusses the triangle-free case. Alon's “Bipartite subgraphs,” reference [6], cites that Erdős paper.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove [CEG79], or replace it with P. Erdős, “Problems and results in graph theory and combinatorial analysis,” Graph Theory and Related Topics (Proc. Waterloo, 1977), Academic Press, 1979, 153–163, especially §8. Retain [Al96], whose Theorem 1.2 supports the formalized bounds.

reformulations.difference: The source describes the largest guaranteed number of edges, whereas Lean takes a natural-number supremum of guarantees expressed using “at least k edges” rather than exactly k.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The set of guarantees contains 0, witnessed by the empty spanning graph. Every guarantee is at most m, by applying it to K_{1,m}; therefore its natural supremum is an attained maximum, with no default-value issue. A bipartite subgraph with at least k edges can have edges deleted to leave exactly k, preserving bipartiteness and inclusion. Scratch Lean proves the maximum property, the at-least/exact equivalence, and equality with the equality-based supremum.

reformulations.difference: Alon's Theorem 1.2 states the lower bound for edge counts greater than 1; Lean states both bounds for every natural edge count, including 0 and 1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The definition gives f(0)=0 and f(1)=1, both proved independently in scratch Lean. Also 0^(4/5)=0. Replace the source's constants by min(c₁,1/2) and max(c₂,1/2): the bounds then hold at 1, remain valid for larger edge counts, and hold automatically at 0. Restricting the Lean statement gives the converse. The equivalence was proved in scratch Lean.

sources_consulted: N. Alon, “Bipartite subgraphs,” Combinatorica 16 (1996), 301–311, especially Theorem 1.2, §3, concluding remarks, and reference [6]: https://web.math.princeton.edu/~nalon/PDFS/bipartite3.pdf
F. R. K. Chung, P. Erdős, and R. L. Graham, “On the product of the point and line covering numbers of a graph” (1979), 597–602: https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1979-16.pdf
P. Erdős, “Problems and results in graph theory and combinatorial analysis” (1979), §8, pp. 159–161: https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1979-17.pdf
Collected Papers of Paul Erdős, publication index: https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/Erdos.html
Linked formal proof at the pinned commit: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plby/lean-proofs/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos581.lean

The linked proof's transitive source files at the same commit: Erdos581/{Basic,StableNumerics,StableCut,Peeling,DenseCore,LowerBound,FourierCut,UpperBlock,UpperSpectrum,UpperPadding,UpperBound}.lean and Erdos127/BalancedCut.lean; inspected relevant definitions and statements, scanned for holes/custom axioms, and rebuilt the complete dependency closure.
review.notes: No mathematical misformalization was found in either declaration. The finite-vertex hypothesis prevents ncard's infinite-set default, and the supremum set is nonempty and bounded. Checks in /workspace/review/scratch.lean include f(0)=0, f(1)=1, f(m)≤m, and the recorded equivalences; finite computations also checked stars and the five-cycle. The pinned external proof and its dependencies rebuilt successfully. Its Nat.findGreatest definition was proved equal to the file's sSup definition, and /workspace/review/external-proof/certify-statement.lean derives the literal repository statement. #print axioms reports only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. Thus the solved and formal_proof metadata are supported. The live https://www.erdosproblems.com/581 page returned a Cloudflare challenge despite descriptive User-Agent headers, so its current page-specific remarks/status wording could not be inspected; the mathematical comparison was made directly against the primary papers. The reviewed file was not modified.
